data.name: Lemuria: Lost in Space - VR Edition
data.detailed_description:
Lemuria: Lost in Space is a unique adventure, full of mysteries, puzzles and shocking discoveries. It's a combination of point 'n click adventure, RPG and survival game.


Play VR edition - with free first-person movement and full HTC Vive support!

  • Explore over 100 rooms of the spaceship, solve dozens of puzzles, find valuable resources and fight with security turrets and other enemies patrolling the ship;
  • Uncover the story of the lost crew of Lemuria 7. The ship has been missing for over 70 years - find out what exactly happened to them;
  • Acquire new skills allowing you to hack computer terminals or even the spaceship network to avoid fighting with patrolling robots;
  • Challenge yourself in demanding mini-games that will test your logical thinking and maths skills;
  • Feel the unique atmosphere of the abandoned spaceship with the original soundtrack, composed by Ree-D.
  • Play now - free demo available.


The Lemuria 7 spaceship has been missing for over 70 years.
Now it is back in the Solar System, however there are no crew members on it. It's also unclear how the Lemuria 7 has returned and why it has been seriously damaged.

In Lemuria: Lost in Space, you play as Abrix - the robot with AI that may operate in extreme temperatures, high levels of radiation and that yields weapon and hacking modules in order to explore the whole ship.


Abrix has an ability to overrun security systems. The unique hacking mini-game will challenge your math, geographic and logical thinking skills. There is no time to check Wikipedia - every mistake costs you valuable resources!

Abrix has a special software that allows him to upgrade himself during the mission. You need to be very careful - if you run out of batteries or an anti-radiation cloak, the mission is aborted and the game is over.


In order to explore over 100 rooms of the spaceship, you'll need to solve dozens of puzzles, find valuable resources for the robot and fight with security turrets and other enemies patrolling the ship.

Solving puzzles not only rewards you with priceless resources, but also uncovers the story of the lost crew of Lemuria 7. The level of challenge depends on difficulty - so choose wisely or you'll need to start from scratch.

The game demo is available now!

FAQ
Q - What is the diffrence between this game and original "Lemuria: Lost in Space"?
A - VR edition is remastered in many ways and now it contains:
- Free first person movement with WASD and controller support,
- Full HTC Vive VR support with intuitive GUI, smart teleportation system, very easy and ready to play fighting system
- Easier to use items
- Bug fixes

Q - My HTC Vive controllers are not working.
A - Turn off the game, go to SteamVR and make sure that controllers are on. Then start the game again.

Q - I can't start the game, Steam tells that it's already running.
A - Restart SteamVR, Steam client, and try to start the game again.

Q - Can I play without VR hardware?
A - You can play on any monitor, without VR hardware - using a mouse and keyboard or a controller.

Q - Do you plan to support diffrent VR hardware than HTC Vive?
A - We are working on porting the game to the next platforms and systems, but we can not promise at this time any specific date.

Q - What are hardware requirements for playing with HTC Vive
A - Graphic: GeForce GTX 970 (AMD Radeon R9 290) or better
CPU: Intel® i5-4590, AMD FX 8350, or better
More: see HTC Vive Steam store page

reviews.review:
Lemuria: Lost in Space – VR Edition is a science-fiction adventure that aims to immerse players in a mysterious journey through the depths of space. Developed and published by EJRGames, the title combines exploration, puzzle-solving, survival mechanics, and light role-playing elements within a virtual reality environment. Rather than focusing on intense action or combat-heavy encounters, the game builds its identity around discovery and investigation, placing players aboard the spacecraft Lemuria as they attempt to uncover the truth behind a catastrophic event that has left the vessel isolated and filled with unanswered questions.

The strongest aspect of the experience is its atmosphere. From the moment players enter the abandoned spacecraft, there is a constant sense of uncertainty and curiosity. The ship itself becomes a character, filled with hidden details, inaccessible areas, and environmental clues that slowly reveal pieces of the story. The game encourages methodical exploration, rewarding those who carefully examine their surroundings instead of rushing toward objectives. This deliberate pacing helps establish tension and gives every new discovery a feeling of importance.

The VR implementation significantly enhances immersion. Walking through dimly lit corridors, inspecting machinery, and interacting with objects directly creates a stronger connection to the environment than a traditional screen-based experience would provide. The sense of scale and presence contributes greatly to the game's appeal, making players feel as though they are genuinely stranded aboard a drifting spacecraft. Even relatively simple tasks become more engaging because of the hands-on nature of virtual reality interaction.

Puzzle-solving serves as one of the central gameplay pillars. Players are frequently required to investigate systems, locate items, and connect clues to progress deeper into the ship. The puzzles generally rely on observation and logical reasoning rather than reflexes, which complements the exploratory nature of the adventure. While some challenges may occasionally feel difficult due to limited guidance, they usually fit naturally within the setting and reinforce the sensation of uncovering a larger mystery piece by piece.

Another interesting aspect is the incorporation of survival and RPG-inspired mechanics. Resource collection and inventory management add a layer of strategic thinking to exploration. These systems are not especially complex, but they provide enough depth to make progression feel meaningful. Instead of simply moving from one puzzle to another, players must also consider what they carry, what resources they possess, and how to prepare for future obstacles. These mechanics help create a more complete experience that extends beyond a traditional adventure game formula.

Visually, Lemuria: Lost in Space – VR Edition succeeds in delivering a believable science-fiction setting despite its independent development origins. The environments feature a variety of technological structures, control rooms, corridors, and maintenance areas that help establish the illusion of a functioning spacecraft. Although the graphical fidelity does not reach the standards of larger-budget VR productions, the environmental design effectively supports the game's themes of isolation, mystery, and survival. The attention given to atmosphere often compensates for technical limitations.

The sound design also contributes substantially to immersion. Ambient noises, mechanical hums, and subtle musical cues create a persistent sense of unease. Rather than relying on loud or dramatic audio, the game uses quieter environmental sounds to reinforce the loneliness of deep space. This restrained approach complements the narrative and helps maintain tension throughout the journey. The result is an experience where audio and visual presentation work together to support exploration and storytelling.

The game is not without flaws. Its slow pace may prove challenging for players expecting frequent action or constant excitement. Certain interactions can feel cumbersome, and some puzzles may require patience before their solutions become clear. Additionally, as an earlier VR-focused title, some control systems and interface elements may feel less refined compared to modern virtual reality standards. These issues occasionally interrupt immersion, though they rarely overshadow the strengths of the overall experience.

What makes Lemuria: Lost in Space – VR Edition memorable is its commitment to creating a thoughtful and atmospheric adventure rather than chasing mainstream trends. It successfully blends mystery, exploration, survival, and puzzle-solving into a cohesive package that rewards curiosity and careful observation. Players who enjoy uncovering hidden stories, exploring detailed environments, and experiencing science-fiction worlds at a measured pace will likely find the journey engaging from beginning to end.

Lemuria: Lost in Space – VR Edition stands as a solid independent VR adventure that prioritizes atmosphere and exploration over spectacle. While its pacing and occasional mechanical roughness prevent it from achieving broader appeal, its intriguing setting, immersive virtual reality implementation, and rewarding sense of discovery make it a worthwhile experience for fans of mystery-driven science-fiction adventures.

Rating: 6/10
